newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Steady despite abundance of offers.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Steady despite abundance of offers.

text.p: An abundance of offers for high sulphur fuel oil kept prices steady despite firmer crude on Tuesday and traders said they did not expect major falls unless crude prices tumble.
"There are more than enough offers at this moment and prices may go down slightly in the short term," said one trader.
"The situation may last until after the Chinese New Year," he added.
Some supplies sold to Chinese buyers who had refused to take the cargoes, continued to make their way back to Singapore, adding supplies in the market, traders said.

In the LSWR market, 100-150,000 March lifting barrels were offered down 25 cents intraday to $20.25 per barrel. Three buyers were also reported seeking March barrels at between $19.70 to $20.25 but no deals were reported.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
MTH FOB SIN BUY/SELL PREV BUY/SELL
In late market talks, two 180-cst February cargoes were offered at $96-$97 per tonne fob Singapore, compared with Monday's offers ranging between $96-$98.
A seller of 380-cst also emerged at $89 per tonne for February lifting. But the higher viscosity cargo also failed to attract any buying interest.
February swaps were largely unchanged at $98.00/$99.25 per tonne amid lacklustre trading interest.
